data.name: Vishalak
data.gender_notes: Vishalak is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Vishala refers to something large or big, and k means a body. Thus, Vishalak means one with a big body. The name Vishalak carries the meaning “One with a big body” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Vishalak usually hope their child will grow to embody one with a big body and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Vishalak belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “One with a big body.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Vishalak total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

data.cultural_impact: The name Vishalak is rooted in the Sanskrit language, which is an integral part of Hindu culture. It is a compound word with the meanings "large" (Vishala) and "body" (k), giving the name Vishalak. In Hindu mythology, gods or beings who possess this trait, such as Vishnu, are often depicted as having immense size and power. This name may have been given to someone who is perceived as having strength, largeness, or a dominant presence in society.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Vishalak is related to the idea of transcending our physical limitations. In Hinduism, it is believed that the soul is eternal and possesses infinite potential. The word "Vishal" signifies "wide" or "extensive," which can represent the vastness of the soul's capacity. Thus, the name Vishalak, which translates to "one with a big body," could symbolize an individual who carries the divine essence within themselves, embodying the infinite nature of the soul, striving towards spiritual growth and enlightenment.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Vishalak: Radiant and expansive, embodiment of boundless joy and love. Symbolizing the limitless nature of the soul and its infinite capacity for growth.
